target: SWE intern / new-grad roles (general software engineering, 2026–27 recruiting cycle)
seven_second_takeaway: UMD CS '28, AWS SDE intern + Capital One SWE intern, Amazon contract work, ML research, campus studio co-founder; Capital One 65% LLM latency cut and 90% dev preference stand out.

score_rationale.impact_clarity: AWS, Bedrock, PhysTwin, search-index and all three IEX bullets end at method or intent; no result or consequence stated.
score_rationale.quantification: 34% and 30% lack a baseline (34% vs what prior architecture? 30% from how long?); IEX benchmark names metrics but reports none.
score_rationale.credibility: IEX bullets read as stacked design jargon ('contract-based plug-in', 'time-based adaptive LSM'); 'targeting ICLR' name-drops without stating own contribution.

must_fix: clarify: 34% Kinesis latency cut — what was the pipeline before (batch? synchronous calls?) and how was end-to-end latency measured; adding Kinesis usually adds hops, so an interviewer will probe this immediately

clarify: IEX project design — 'paginated hash-based order-book storage' and 'time-based adaptive LSM store' are unusual choices for an order book; reword in plain terms you can defend, and state what the benchmark found (if you have it) or cut the bullet
clarify: PhysTwin bullet — say what you personally built for 'automated training'; 'on a PhD-led team targeting ICLR' currently carries the bullet and invites 'what did you do?'

bullets.quote: Tuning Java-based upper/lower bounds on EC2 capacity
bullets.issue: Lone AWS bullet is in-progress and vague; 'tuning bounds' could mean editing config constants.
bullets.suggestion: Tuning Java-based upper/lower bounds on EC2 capacity reserved for Redshift maintenance (e.g. patching), backtesting policies against historical demand to balance availability and cost

bullets.quote: Rebuilt a legacy test-data workflow builder in React/TypeScript
Built a precomputed tree-style search index over popular
bullets.issue: Ends at intent ('to minimize DB queries'); no outcome. Accepted risk, but still the weakest Capital One bullet.
bullets.suggestion: Consider merging into the LLM-latency bullet as one of its search tools, so it borrows that bullet's outcome instead of standing alone without one

bullets.quote: Cut LLM workflow generation time 65% to under
bullets.issue: 'Claude skill' is jargon to a recruiter; otherwise strong with clear baseline implied.
bullets.suggestion: Cut LLM workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by splitting one monolithic Claude prompt/skill into sub-skills backed by Python search and validation tools, guided by CloudWatch + OpenSearch latency logs

Reduced end-to-end latency 34% for a pipeline
bullets.issue: Baseline architecture missing; 'moving onto Kinesis' reducing latency needs the 'from what' to be believable.
bullets.suggestion: Reduced end-to-end latency 34% for a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research documents to inference by replacing [prior approach] with Kinesis streams feeding Lambda processors

bullets.quote: Automated fine-tuning of an AWS Bedrock source-relevancy model
bullets.issue: Tech list after the semicolon; no stated outcome of the decision gates.
bullets.suggestion: Automated scheduled fine-tuning of a Bedrock source-relevancy model (EventBridge cron) with decision gates that skip retraining when data hasn't meaningfully changed; added X-Ray tracing and SNS failure alerts

bullets.quote: Developing automated training for PhysTwin, a physics-based digital
bullets.issue: Own contribution unclear; 'targeting ICLR' does the heavy lifting.
bullets.suggestion: Building [your specific component] that automates training runs for PhysTwin, a physics-based digital twin, on a PhD-led team preparing an ICLR submission

bullets.quote: Engineered a Python pipeline rendering AnyGrasp multi-camera grasp
Shortened research-environment setup time 30% with uv dependency
bullets.issue: 30% lacks baseline; second clause (profiling, Pytest) is a separate unrelated task.
bullets.suggestion: Cut research-environment setup time 30% (state from X min) via uv dependency pinning and Docker; added psutil time/memory profiling and Pytest suites to locate pipeline bottlenecks

bullets.quote: Co-founded a 110+ member campus product studio that
bullets.issue: 'run with Jira and GitHub' is filler; what was your engineering role across the 5 products?
bullets.suggestion: Co-founded a 110+ member campus product studio that has shipped 5 live products

bullets.quote: Wrote Prisma SQL queries and Redis query caching
bullets.issue: 20,000+ visits is product traction, not your result; DB load reduction unquantified.
bullets.suggestion: Built the Prisma query layer and Redis caching for Tortuga, a class scheduler that drew 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days, cutting repeated DB reads under launch traffic

bullets.quote: Building a RAG meal-suggestion feature for the official
bullets.issue: Tester count unknown (accepted risk); 'internal testers' scoping is honest.

bullets.issue: 'contract-based plug-in interface... enforced correctness' sounds LLM-polished; say plainly what's swappable and how correctness is checked.
bullets.suggestion: Implemented a C++ order-book simulator that replays historical IEX data, with a plug-in interface for swapping matching/storage strategies and invariant checks on every replayed event

bullets.quote: Designed paginated hash-based order-book storage with an in-memory
bullets.issue: Unusual design for an order book; 'checked for drift' is the only result and is vague.
bullets.suggestion: Designed hash-based paged order-book storage with an LFU cache for hot tickers, validating reconstructed books against IEX historical snapshots

bullets.quote: Benchmarked a time-based adaptive LSM store against a
bullets.issue: Benchmark with no finding; 'time-based adaptive LSM' is undefined jargon.
bullets.suggestion: If results exist, state which won and by how much; otherwise merge into the previous bullet or cut to save a line

structure.change: Trim IEX project to two plainly-worded bullets, or cut the benchmark bullet if no result exists
structure.rationale: Three jargon-dense, result-free bullets weaken an otherwise credible page; quant-style projects get grilled hardest.

structure.change: Drop bold on '270K+ row' and '110+ member'; keep bold only on outcome metrics
structure.rationale: Bold should mark results; scale/context numbers dilute the headline wins.

top3: clarify: the 34% Kinesis latency baseline (what the pipeline replaced) so the number survives one follow-up question
Rewrite the IEX project in plain, defensible language and state benchmark findings or cut that bullet
Make PhysTwin and AWS bullets name your own concrete contribution instead of leaning on 'ICLR' and 'tuning bounds'
